paper.title_en: A perturbative Liouville prescription for the celestial three-gluon amplitude
paper.abstract_en: We study the celestial three-point Mellin representation for three-gluon scattering in a dilaton background within the Mellin--Liouville formulation of Stieberger, Taylor and Zhu (STZ). We formulate an alternative perturbative prescription in which the light Liouville parameters are kept fixed in the small-$b$ expansion. Requiring global conformal covariance, a controlled light-operator expansion of the Liouville DOZZ structure constant, and consistency with the standard celestial three-gluon representation fixes the corresponding Mellin-Liouville map and operator normalization. Starting from the full Liouville three-point function, we derive the leading and first subleading terms in the $b^2$ expansion. The leading term reproduces the standard tree-level celestial Yang--Mills representation in the appropriate small-total-momentum limit, while the first subleading term is interpreted as the first coefficient of a controlled Liouville deformation of this tree-level construction. We develop an operator representation of the inverse Mellin transform, whereby polynomial dependence on the Mellin parameters is converted into differential operators acting on the leading Mellin integral. The resulting subleading contribution is obtained in closed form in terms of modified Bessel functions, with characteristic logarithmic and nonanalytic behaviour at small total momentum. Finally, we clarify the relation between the fixed-$σ$ and STZ finite-$b$ parametrizations by deriving the induced nonlinear reparametrization of the Mellin dimension and its action on the inverse Mellin representation. The result provides a systematic framework for studying finite-$b$ Liouville deformations and their possible relation to perturbative structures in celestial Yang-Mills theory.
